TRIPARTITE STRUGGLE AND CHOLAS

Tripartite Struggle

  • It is also known as Kannauj Triangle Wars that took place between Palas, Pratiharas, and Rashtrakutas during 8th and 10th Centuries.

PALA DYNASTY

  • Founder: Gopala (founder of Odantapuri University)
  • Son: Dharmapala (founder of Vikramshila University (Bhagalpur, Bihar).
  • He also defeated Indrayudh and conquered Kannauj for a brief time.
  • The Palas ruled over Bengal region.
  • They were followers of Mahayana Buddhism.
  • Rulers: Gopala → Dharmapala → Devapala → Mahipala → Ramapala
  • They were the followers of Mahayana Buddhism.
  • Sena Dynasty ruled Bengal after Pala Dynasty (11th-12th century AD).
  • During Sena Dynasty rule Jayadeva wrote Gita Govinda.

GURJARA PRATIHARA

  • Founder: Nagabhatta I
  • Capital: Kannauj/Bhinmal

Nagabhatta II

  • He defeated Dharmapala but was defeated by Govinda III (Rashtrakuta ruler).
Note: Do not get confused between the early Cholas that ruled during Sangam Age (3rd Century BC-3rd Century AD) and later Cholas, who ruled between 9th and 13th Century AD.

Mihir Bhoja (836 CE-885 CE)

  • He was praised by the Arabian Scholar Sulaiman for keeping his empire safe from robbers.
  • Sulaiman was an Arab traveler who visited during his reign and described his military power, riches and efficient administration.

Mahendrapala

  • Rajashekhara was his court poet.

CHOLA DYNASTY (850 AD-1280 AD)

  • Founder: Vijayalaya Chola
  • They were feudatories to Pallavas.
  • He captured Tanjore/Thanjavur from Muttaraiyars (Kaveri Delta).
  • He also built a temple for goddess Nishumbhasudeni.

Prantaka I (907 AD-955 AD)

  • He defeated Pandyas at Vellore.
  • He lost to Rashtrakuta king Krishna III who made a Victory Pillar and Krishneshwara temple at Rameshwaram.

Raja Raja I (985 AD-1014 AD)

  • He defeated Cheras at Trivandrum and conquered Madurai from Pandyas.
  • He conquered Maldives and invaded Sri Lanka.
  • He encouraged the Sailendra ruler of Sri Vijayapuram to build a Buddhist Vihara at Nagapattinam.

Rajendra I (1012 AD-1044 AD)

  • He was the son of Raja Raja I.
  • He is also known as "Napoleon of South India".
  • He completely conquered Sri Lankan (Ceylon) capital Anuradhapur.
  • Mahmud of Ghazni was his contemporary.
  • He crossed Ganga and defeated two local Kings of Bengal and took the title "Gangaikondachola" and built the city → Gangaikondacholapuram.
  • Chola fought against Chalukyas of Kalyani.
  • Chola empire declined during early part of 13th Century.
  • The place of Cholas was taken by Pandyas and Hoysalas.
  • The place of late Chalukyas was taken by Yadavas and Kakatiyas.

Administration

  • The king of Chola Dynasty has all the authority.
  • He had Council of Ministers to advice him.
  • Chola Empire was divided into: Mandalams (province) which was further divided into Valandu (districts) and Nadus (villages or sub-districts).

Chola Government

  • Cholas are known for local (decentralised)/village government.

TRIPARTITE STRUGGLE AND CHOLAS

  • There were two assemblies:
  • Ur: Assembly of common people.
  • Sabha: Assembly of learned Brahmins (Agrahara: Land of Brahmins).
  • Affairs of the village were managed by an executive committee. People with property or land were privileged to take part in the elections (Uttaramerur Inscription).

Yadava Dynasty

  • Capital: Devagiri

Hoysala Dynasty

  • Capital: Halebidu
  • Famous for star-shaped temple.

Kakatiyas

  • Capital: Warangal

Land Donations

TypePurpose
BrahmadeyaLand donated to Brahmans
VellanvagaiLand donated to non-Brahmans/Peasants
DevadanaLand donated to temples
PallichchhandamLand donated to Jain community
ShalabhogaLand donated for maintenance of school

Tax

  • There were two types of taxes governed by Chola Empire: Vetti (forced labour) and Kadamai (land revenue tax).

Great Living Chola Temples

  • All the temples under this category are listed in UNESCO World Heritage Site.
  • Brihadeeshwara Temple is built at:
  • Tanjore, by Raja Raja I (also known as Rajarajeshwara Temple).
  • Gangaikonda Cholapuram at Tamil Nadu, by Rajendra I.
  • Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram, built by Raja Raja II.

Temple Architecture

  • Nagara style (in North India), Dravida style (in South India), and Vesara style (a mixture of Nagara and Dravida style).

Nagara Style vs Dravida Style:

Nagara StyleDravida Style
It is commonly found in: Northern and Central regions of IndiaIt is commonly found in Southern India
Main shrine: Shikhara which is curvilinear or conical in shapeMain shrine: Vimana
Gopuram (main entrance) is not present hereGopuram is present here
Mandapa (pillared hall) is connected to Sanctum and features a pyramidal or conical roofMandapa is connected to Sanctum and has flat-roofed assembly hall
Nandi is placed inside the templeNandi is placed outside the temple
Chief deity is installed at Garbhagriha (Sanctum Sanctorum)Chief deity is installed at Garbhagriha
A water tank or reservoir may or may not be presentThe temples consists of large water reservoirs or temple tanks inside temple complex
They are not made on apsidal planeThey are made on an apsidal plane (elliptical in shape) known as Gaja Pristha
  • In early 11th century, the Chola king Rajendra I built a Shiva temple and filled it with Sun-pedestal seized from the Chalukyas, a Ganesha statue and several statues of Durga; a Nandi statue from the Eastern Chalukyas; an image of Bhairava (a form of Shiva) and Bhairavi from the Kalinga of Orissa; and a Kali statue from the Palas of Bengal (Brihadeeshwara temple).

Some Other Temples

  • This temple is a part of Khajuraho temples).
  • Built by: Chandela Dynasty rulers.
  • Walls of temple depict the Kamasutra of Vatsyayana.
  • Natraj performing Tandava.
  • The figurine is made of Bronze using Lost Wax Technique.
The Cholas were known for their splendid Bronze sculptures made through Lost Wax Technique.

Other Architecture of Various Dynasties

  • It is also known as Black Pagoda
  • Built by: Narasingha Deva I (Eastern Ganga Dynasty)
  • Style: Nagara + Kalinga style.
  • It is seen in 10₹ note.
  • Earliest temple (Vimal Vasahi, 1031 AD) built by Vimal Shah (Jain minister of Solanki king Bhima I); Luna Vasahi (1230 AD) built by Vastupala-Tejapala brothers (corrected: attribution to "Vastupala brothers" alone omits Vimal Shah, who built the earliest and most prominent temple).
  • Style: Maru Gurjara style (developed by Solankis → Feudatories of Chalukyas in Western India).
  • Style: Maru Gurjara style.
  • Built by: King Bhimadeva I of Solanki Dynasty.
  • Style: Maru Gurjara style.
  • This temple is also known as White Pagoda.
  • Style: Rekha Deula style
  • Built by: Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva (Eastern Ganga Dynasty).
